missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative predicate. 'Взрыв' is the masculine nominative subject. 'Сильный' is the agreeing masculine adjective and 'очень' intensifies it. A basic descriptive model.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Взрыв' is the accusative direct object of 'услышали'; inanimate masculine accusative equals the nominative. 'Громкий' agrees in the masculine accusative.
Strategic focus: Genitive with preposition. 'Взрыва' is genitive after 'после', marking time. The impersonal 'было тихо' describes the aftermath. A useful sequence-of-events pattern.
Strategic focus: Genitive of relation. 'Взрыва' is the genitive modifying 'причина', the cause of what. 'Пока' adds a temporal note. Common in news language.
Strategic focus: Instrumental of means. 'Взрывом' is the instrumental showing the agent of destruction. 'Мощным' agrees in the masculine instrumental. A passive-style construction.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'Взрыве' is prepositional after 'при', meaning during the event. 'Газа' is a genitive modifier. A grim but frequent news pattern.

missions.phrase: Журналисты пишут о взрыве на заводе.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Prepositional topic. 'Взрыве' is prepositional after 'о', the topic of the article. 'На заводе' adds the location. Useful for reporting events.
Strategic focus: Dative with preposition. 'Взрыву' is dative after 'к', expressing what one prepares for. 'Новому' agrees in the masculine dative. A planning-for-danger pattern.
Strategic focus: Genitive singular after a numeral. The numeral 'два' governs the genitive singular 'взрыва'. 'В городе' sets the scene. A common quantity construction.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural. 'Взрывов' is the genitive plural after 'несколько', expressing an indefinite count. 'Ночью' adds the time. Good practice for the masculine plural ending.
